correctness.rationale: For q>p>1 coprime odd, the canonical continued-fraction product M(c_0)...M(c_m) has first column (q,p) and second (u,v) with pu-qv=(-1)^m. Its penultimate convergent produces the positive solution a=u for even m, a=q-u for odd m, hence a≡u+m (mod 2). Mod 2, an even quotient gives a transposition and an odd quotient a 3-cycle in GL2(F2)≅S3; the final first column (1,1) shows u≡1+#even_quotients. Therefore a≡#odd_quotients≡Σc_i (mod2). Since ap-bq=1 and p,q odd, a,b have opposite parity. Renshaw Lemma 4 gives each cross intersection (h±1)/2, with h=n/(pq) odd; his two-prime inclusion-exclusion then yields T=(S-1+2δ)/2 where δ=+1 iff a odd, giving exactly (S+1)/2 for odd quotient sum and (S-3)/2 otherwise. All exponents e,f≥1 are included because only h changes, not its parity or the sign criterion.
